title: Sales enablement playbook: positioning, competitive briefs, pitch decks, pricing & security FAQ
author: Elena Martinez
summary: Unified playbook for Redwood field and SDR teams to position the Redwood Inference platform, handle competitive conversations, assemble pitch decks, present pricing guidance, and respond to prospect security questions. Includes a short case study and canned battlecards.
audience: Sales, Solutions Engineering, SDRs, Sales Leadership, Customer Success
body:
Overview

Purpose
- Provide a one-stop reference for messaging, competitive talking points, pitch-deck structure, pricing guardrails, and security FAQ tailored for prospects evaluating inference platforms.
- Align GTM teams on consistent claims, measurable outcomes, and escalation paths for technical questions.

Positioning & Core Messaging

Elevator pitch (30s)
Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform that delivers predictable, high-performance LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments 

- letting engineering teams ship LLM features with production-grade latency, reliability, and predictable unit economics.

Value pillars (customer-facing)
1) Production performance: predictable latency and throughput with GPU-optimized runtime, continuous batching, and KV caching to meet low-latency SLOs.
2) Cost control: intelligent batching, caching, and quantization guidance to reduce per-token cost while preserving quality.
3) Unified operations: same API and rollout tools across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments for fast iteration and safe rollouts.
4) Enterprise readiness: SLAs, private deployment options (VPC/on-prem), KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logging.

Target personas and tailored messages
- Product/ML Engineers: emphasize runtime reliability, SDKs, and per-route observability.
- Platform/Infra teams: emphasize dedicated capacity, private deployment, and network/KMS controls.
- Engineering leadership: emphasize unit economics, predictable spend, and migration path from PoC to dedicated capacity.
- Security/Compliance: emphasize private control plane, audit logs, SOC2/ISO alignment, and data residency options.

Positioning vs. category alternatives
- Compared to turnkey LLM APIs: Redwood offers stronger controls for latency and cost with flexible deployment modes.
- Compared to self-hosted runtimes: Redwood reduces operational burden with a managed control plane, verified performance profiles, and rollout tooling.

Competitive Briefs / Battlecards (short form)

Competitors covered: OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Replicate/self-hosted runtimes

OpenAI
- Strengths: industry-leading model quality, broad ecosystem adoption, simple API.
- Weaknesses: limited control over deployment topology, variable unit economics at scale, fewer on-prem/private deployment options.
- Redwood counter-plays: highlight dedicated capacity and predictable pricing, private deployment for regulated customers, per-route observability and cost breakdowns.

Anthropic
- Strengths: safety-focused models and research reputation.
- Weaknesses: fewer deployment modes and less tooling for cost optimization.
- Redwood counter-plays: emphasize operational tooling (rollouts, tracing), model catalog with performance profiles, and cost-performance tooling.

AWS Bedrock
- Strengths: deep cloud integration, enterprise contracts.
- Weaknesses: vendor lock-in concerns, variable latency across regions, limited on-prem options.
- Redwood counter-plays: selling point is neutral model catalog + private deployment options and predictable dedicated capacity with SLOs.

Self-hosted runtimes / Replicate
- Strengths: full control, potentially lower raw compute costs.
- Weaknesses: heavy ops burden, engineering maintenance, and lack of standardized observability/rollout patterns.
- Redwood counter-plays: accelerate time-to-production, reduce ops through managed control plane and proven runtime optimizations.

Common objection handling
- "We can host it ourselves cheaper." -> Run-through PoC cost comparison template (link) and highlight total cost of ownership: ops headcount, time to iterate, reliability incidents.
- "We need on-prem/offline." -> Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packaging; outline implementation checklist (networking, KMS, air-gap plan).

Pitch Deck Guidance (recommended slide outline)
1) Title / Team / One-liner
2) Problem statement: specific latency/cost/reliability pain for LLM features
3) Why existing options fail: examples and data points (latency spikes, ops time)
4) Redwood solution: short architecture diagram (hosted/dedicated/private), bullets on runtime features (batching, KV cache, kernel selection)
5) Metrics & guarantees: SLOs, latency percentiles, expected throughput curves for standard instance types
6) Cost story: per-token comparisons, batching-related savings, dedicated vs hosted economics
7) Security & compliance: deployment modes, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC2/ISO statements
8) Case study: metrics and timeline (see below)
9) Deployment plan & next steps: pilot scope, success criteria, timeline, roles
10) Pricing & commercial ask: recommend next step (trial, dedicated capacity assessment)

Pitching tips
- Keep first call technical: include SE early if prospect mentions latency/throughput.
- Use customer metrics: replace generic numbers with prospect\u2019s expected qps/latency for credibility.
- Bring the runtime: run a quick smoke demo using their prompt set to demonstrate latency and cost.

Pricing guidance (guardrails)

Pricing models we sell
- Hosted usage-based: per-token generation and embedding units with tiered discounts by volume.
- Dedicated capacity: monthly reserved GPU capacity (commit) with predictable throughput and overage/burst options.
- Private deployment licensing: platform fee + optional support/maintenance contracts.

How to recommend pricing options
- Early PoC (<100k tokens/day): start with hosted usage to lower time-to-value.
- Scaling applications (>500k tokens/day or strict latency SLOs): evaluate Dedicated for predictable throughput and improved unit economics.
- Regulated or air-gapped workloads: Private deployment + support contract.

Discounting and commercial playbook
- Standard discount bands tied to annual committed spend.
- Erosion policy: single-cycle approval for up to 20% ACV discount from list; sales leader approval required above.
- Bundles: include onboarding credits, extended observability data retention, and premium SLAs as negotiation levers.

Contracting and procurement notes
- Typical timeline: 4\u20138 weeks for dedicated or private procurement (security review + network work).
- Required legal artifacts: DPA, SOC2 attestation, standard SOW for dedicated/on-prem installations.

Case study (concise)

Customer: FinTech payments platform (anonymous: "Confidio")
- Problem: Frequent latency spikes during peak load and unpredictable inference spend impacting fraud detection windows.
- Engagement: 8-week pilot using Redwood hosted API with customer prompt sets, then 3-month Dedicated reservation.
- Outcomes:
  - Latency: 95th percentile reduced from 450ms -> 120ms for the fraud model endpoint.
  - Cost: per-transaction inference cost reduced by ~38% via batching and KV caching.
  - Reliability: Production incidents related to inference dropped to zero during peak trading hours.
- Implementation notes: SE-led smoke test, one-week load test, then staged migration over two sprints.

Security FAQ for prospects (concise Q&A)

Q: Where does customer data reside?
A: For Hosted customers data is stored in region selected at onboarding; logs and artifacts adhere to retention policies. For Dedicated and Private, data can remain in customer VPC or on-prem as configured.

Q: Do you support KMS/HSM?
A: Yes. Redwood integrates with popular KMS providers (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) and offers HSM options for Private deployments.

Q: What compliance certifications do you hold?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and is pursuing ISO 27001. We provide auditors with evidence as part of enterprise diligence.

Q: How do you handle access control and RBAC?
A: Role-based access controls with SSO/SAML and fine-grained API keys. Audit logs capture token-level usage and model access.

Q: Can you run in air-gapped environments?
A: Yes \u2014 the Private on-prem package supports air-gapped installations; contact Engineering for the installation checklist and timeline.

Q: How do you ensure model integrity and supply chain safety?
A: Model artifacts are cryptographically signed, verified at onboarding, and stored in secure registries. We track lineage and provide hashes in deployment manifests.

Q: What is your incident response process?
A: We follow the standard incident-response runbook: detection -> triage -> customer notification per SLA -> postmortem with remediation plan. Enterprise customers receive a dedicated on-call path and status updates.

Operational playbook for trials & pilots (high-level)
1) Intake & discovery: capture target endpoints, expected qps, latency SLOs, and sample prompts.
2) Baseline: run 48\u201372h smoke test using prospect prompts in hosted sandbox to collect latency/cost profiles.
3) Optimization: enable batching/KV cache and recommended quantization profile; measure improvements.
4) Pilot review: present results, recommended next step (hosted vs dedicated), and success criteria.
5) Commercial proposal: include pricing options and recommended contract term.

Appendix: sample one-page battlecard (text)
- Company: Redwood Inference
- One-liner: Developer-first inference platform for predictable performance and cost across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
- Top 3 strengths: Performance SLOs, deployment flexibility, cost optimization tooling.
- Top 3 weak spots: Newer than hyperscalers on brand recognition, model-hosting ecosystem smaller than cloud marketplaces.
- Best fit: Engineering-led buyers who need predictable latency and cost at scale.
